source_name: Erste Group Bank AG — Investor Relations portal
why_relevant: Hub for Erste Group's quarterly investor information, presentations, webcasts and group key financials. Erste reports Hungary as a named geographic segment (Erste Bank Hungary), including loan growth, NII, and the Hungarian bank levy / windfall tax charges — the analytical layer that the Hungarian statutory report lacks.

source_name: Erste Group IR News — dated investor-information releases (quarterly results)
why_relevant: Per-quarter release pages carrying the headline numbers and the links to the results presentation/report. Date-stamped URL pattern (/investorinformation/{yyyy}/{mm}/{dd}/irnews-…) makes them enumerable and gives an exact publication cadence for the Hungary commentary.

source_name: Erste Group Financial Reports section (annual + interim reports)
why_relevant: Full annual and interim financial reports containing the audited geographic segment note where Hungary is a reportable segment — the authoritative version of the country P&L and balance-sheet splits used to reconcile presentation slides.

source_name: Erste Group Annual Report downloads — XLS/XLSX data files
why_relevant: Machine-readable spreadsheet versions of the annual report tables. Where present, these give segment/country figures without PDF table-extraction error — the single highest-value structured artefact in this cell.

source_name: Erste Group annual report filed with Bucharest Stock Exchange (BVB infocont)
why_relevant: Erste is dual-listed (Vienna, Prague, Bucharest); the BVB regulatory filing archive mirrors the full annual report as a stable, non-bot-defended PDF. Useful redundancy when erstegroup.com assets move, and a timestamped regulatory copy.

source_name: Raiffeisen Bank International — Results & Reports (quarterly/semi-annual PDFs)
why_relevant: RBI reports Hungary as a named country segment inside Central Europe, with NII, net commission income (explicitly broken out for clearing/settlement/payment services and FX — directly payments-relevant), loan volumes and risk costs. Highest-value payments KPI text in the whole cell.

source_name: Raiffeisen Bank International — corporate/IR site root
why_relevant: Entry point to RBI's investor section, presentation archive and network-bank descriptions; RBI's Hungarian subsidiary is its oldest CEE network bank, so group strategy statements about Hungary originate here.

source_name: UniCredit Group Results (investor relations, quarterly presentation set)
why_relevant: Canonical index for UniCredit's quarterly results package. Hungary sits inside the CEE division perimeter (Czechia & Slovakia, Hungary, Slovenia, Croatia, Romania, Bulgaria, BiH, Serbia); CEE country slides carry net profit, revenue, loan/deposit volumes and digital KPIs for UniCredit Bank Hungary.

source_name: UniCredit Fixed Income & ESG presentation (quarterly)
why_relevant: A second, deeper quarterly deck aimed at debt investors — typically carries more granular per-country funding, asset-quality and balance-sheet detail for CEE entities than the equity results deck, including Hungary.

source_name: UniCredit Annual Report / Investors hub
why_relevant: Annual reports and consolidated reports carrying the audited segment note for the CEE division and, in the annexes, entity-level data on UniCredit Bank Hungary. Anchor for multi-year time series.

source_name: Intesa Sanpaolo Investor Relations — results & press releases
why_relevant: Intesa reports CIB Bank Hungary inside the International Subsidiary Banks Division. Quarterly consolidated-results press releases and the accompanying decks carry ISBD country breakdowns; Hungary-tagged press releases exist as a dedicated tag on the IR site.

source_name: Intesa Sanpaolo IR press-release archive — Hungary-tagged releases
why_relevant: Demonstrates that Intesa's IR press-release archive is topically indexed and reaches back over a decade, including Hungary-specific announcements (capital injections, restructurings, CIB milestones). Good for building the historical event timeline behind CIB Bank.

source_name: Santander Consumer Finance S.A. — Annual & Interim Reports
why_relevant: SCF is the intermediate parent for Santander's consumer-finance entities across Europe. Its consolidated annual accounts list subsidiaries and geographic breakdowns, which is the place to confirm or deny a Hungarian entity and, if present, size it. Note: the country lists surfaced in the 2024 accounts did not name Hungary — this source is as valuable for disconfirming as for confirming.

source_name: Banco Santander — Annual Financial Report (group, shareholders & investors)
why_relevant: Ultimate parent disclosure layer above SCF. Its annual financial report subsidiary annex is the authoritative check for any Santander-controlled Hungarian entity; also the fallback if SCF changes its reporting perimeter.

source_name: Cofidis Group / Crédit Mutuel Alliance Fédérale — new parent of Magyar Cetelem Bank
why_relevant: OWNERSHIP CORRECTION for this cell: Magyar Cetelem Bank Zrt. is no longer a BNP Paribas Personal Finance subsidiary — Cofidis Group (Crédit Mutuel Alliance Fédérale) completed its acquisition in October 2024. Forward-looking parent-IR coverage of Hungarian consumer credit must therefore track Crédit Mutuel / BFCM investor disclosures, not BNP Paribas.

source_name: BNP Paribas Personal Finance corporate site (historical Cetelem Hungary layer)
why_relevant: Still useful for the pre-2024 history of Magyar Cetelem and for BNP Paribas' remaining Hungarian footprint (BNP Paribas Budapest branch, corporate & institutional banking), which is disclosed only at a coarse geography level in BNP's Universal Registration Document.

source_name: Cbonds issuer page — BNP Paribas Budapest
why_relevant: Aggregator holding issuer profiles, credit ratings and accounting/financial report tables for Hungarian bank entities of foreign groups. Useful as a cross-check on entity identity and reporting history where the parent gives little country detail. Partly paywalled.

source_name: Quartr — IR aggregator (KBC, Erste, RBI, UniCredit profiles)
why_relevant: Aggregates earnings dates, filings, presentations, live and recorded earnings calls and transcripts for all four listed parents in this cell. Highest value is the earnings-call audio/transcript layer, where analysts ask Hungary-specific questions (tax, rate cap, loan demand) whose answers never appear in written reports.

source_name: financialreports.eu — European issuer filings index (Erste, RBI)
why_relevant: Third-party index of European issuers' regulated filings; useful as an independent discovery/liveness channel for parent annual and interim reports when issuer sites restructure their asset paths (a recurring problem with the KBC and RBI CDN-token URLs).

source_name: Portfolio.hu — Hungarian financial press coverage of parent-group results
why_relevant: Hungarian business press reads the Vienna/Brussels/Milan releases the day they land and converts them into HUF-denominated Hungary-only stories (e.g. Raiffeisen Hungary H1 profit falling from HUF 46bn to HUF 12bn; K&H's ~HUF 15bn interest-cap loss). Fastest local-language signal that a parent has published Hungary numbers, and provides HUF framing the parent reports omit.

source_name: Privátbankár.hu — Hungarian coverage of foreign parents' Hungarian results
why_relevant: Second independent Hungarian outlet tracking parent-group disclosures about Hungarian levies and subsidiary results; useful for triangulating Portfolio.hu and for catching stories Portfolio paywalls.

source_name: K&H Bank — éves, féléves és negyedéves jelentések (subsidiary report index)
why_relevant: The Hungarian-language statutory counterpart to KBC's group segment disclosure. Needed to reconcile KBC's EUR-denominated K&H segment line with the HUF statutory accounts, and to pick up Hungarian-only detail (local levies, IFRS vs. local GAAP differences).

source_name: Earnings-call transcript mirrors (Investing.com, Seeking Alpha, Yahoo Finance)
why_relevant: Q&A on parent earnings calls is where Hungary-specific colour is given — bank-levy quantification (e.g. EUR 189m charged in Hungary in Q2 2026 incl. EUR 121m full-year banking tax), interest-cap extension effects, retail loan momentum. These mirrors are the most searchable rendering of that dialogue.

source_name: MNB Közzétételek – advanced search (részletes kereső)
why_relevant: Query surface over the whole OAM corpus: filter by issuer, disclosure type, date. This is the practical entry point for building an incremental harvester of Hungarian banking/payment issuer filings.

source_name: MNB short-selling disclosure register (ssrregister.mnb.hu)
why_relevant: Statutory net-short-position register under the EU Short Selling Regulation; reveals institutional positioning against Hungarian listed banks (OTP in particular) and the identity of foreign funds active in the HU financial sector.

source_name: Elektronikus Beszámoló Portál (e-beszámoló, Igazságügyi Minisztérium)
why_relevant: Every Hungarian Zrt/Kft/Nyrt must deposit its statutory annual accounts here. This is the single highest-leverage source for the long tail of the payments ecosystem: PSP subsidiaries, ATM/cash-in-transit operators, POS and terminal vendors' Hungarian entities, fintech Kft-s, savings cooperatives — entities that have no IR site at all. Filings include mérleg, eredménykimutatás, kiegészítő melléklet and auditor's report.

source_name: e-beszámoló – 'Beszámoló állomány értékesítése' (bulk filing dataset for sale)
why_relevant: Official, licensed route to the entire corpus of deposited Hungarian annual accounts in bulk — the compliant alternative to scraping and the backbone for any longitudinal financial dataset on HU banking/payments companies.

source_name: Céginformációs és az Elektronikus Cégeljárásban Közreműködő Szolgálat (Céginformációs Szolgálat)
why_relevant: The state body that receives filings and defines what company information is public and how it is obtained (free vs. paid, OBR submission route). Its pages are the authoritative map of the Hungarian filing infrastructure and link onward to e-beszámoló, Cégközlöny and e-cégjegyzék.
